baselined_with_reason.scripts/draft_interpretive_claims_2026_0: Skips a topic with no pooled outcome. baselined_with_reason.scripts/sweep_mixed_measure_pools_2026_0: Skips a pool whose entries declare no measure. THE ABSENCE IS THE PROPERTY: a pool with nothing to mix cannot mix measure types. It is also COUNTED rather than dropped -- the sweep reports 79 pools with entries out of 175, so the denominator it checked is stated instead of implied, and the 96 it could not check are visible as a number rather than as silence.

Skips a pool whose measures are all one type. That is the CLEAN case and the whole point of the sweep; reporting it would be reporting every pool in the corpus. The grading function returns None only when the set of measures is homogeneous, which is a positive property computed from the measures themselves, not an absence. The sweep exits PROOF FAILED unless it finds the case CHK018_MIXED_POOLING found, so a grading function that silently returned None for everything would fail the run.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/sweep_abstract_omits_withdrawn_2: Skips a topic where every unpublished outcome IS already mentioned in the abstract. That is the clean case and it is the whole point of the sweep -- reporting it would report every topic that is fine. The property is computed positively: `unmentioned` is built by testing each unpublished outcome's id against the abstract text, so an empty list means each one was found, not that none was looked for. NOT AN UNCOUNTED SKIP: the run exits PROOF FAILED unless it finds sglt2-hf, the case a blind cross-family read found independently, so a sweep whose predicate silently matched nothing would fail rather than report zero.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/audit_abstract_certainty_source_: Skips a topic with no results block. THE ABSENCE IS THE PROPERTY: this audit asks what an abstract's certainty claim was composed FROM, and an object with no outcomes composes no such claim. Nothing is excluded from a fix -- the audit's own denominator is printed (`TOPICS WHOSE ABSTRACT COMPOSES A CERTAINTY CLAIM`), so the set it did not examine is visible as a number rather than as silence.

Skips a topic whose results carry no grade block at all, which is the majority. The positive property is stated and counted: only topics that DO compose a certainty claim are judged, and that count is printed. The audit exits non-zero when any judged topic disagrees with its GRADE record, so a broken lookup that made every topic look unjudgeable would report 0 examined -- visible, not silent.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/gate_paper_reads_as_prose_2026_0: Skips a delivered page with no `id="paper"` panel -- 40 pages in this corpus carry none, by design. A page with no manuscript has no prose to judge, and the gate prints PAPERS JUDGED so the number it read is stated beside the number that failed. Its `prove()` runs before every scan and refuses to proceed unless each pattern fires on its own case and none fires on clean prose, so a scan that silently judged nothing would still have to pass a proof that it can detect anything at all.
Skips a topic that publishes no pooled outcome. THE ABSENCE IS THE PROPERTY AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE MEASUREMENT: this audit exists because the previous one counted GRADE PER PAGE, and a topic with no pool has no pool to rate. The denominator it did examine is printed on every run -- 34 pooled outcomes across 28 topics -- so the set it skipped is visible as arithmetic rather than as silence, which is the exact failure the per-page count made.

Skips a not-pooled outcome that carries no rating in the location being examined, because an outcome with no rating cannot be a STRANDED rating. The positive property is computed: `stranded` collects only outcomes that DO hold a value while that topic's pooled outcomes hold none in the same location. The run exits non-zero when that set is non-empty, and it currently does -- sglt2-hf, results.*.grade=HIGH on an outcome marked not pooled -- so this guard is demonstrably not swallowing the condition it stands next to.
baselined_with_reason.scripts/audit_writers_guard_authored_pro: SELECTION, NOT EXCLUSION-BY-ABSENCE. The population this audit measures is 'files that WRITE an object' -- detected positively by `atomic_write.write_json`, `json.dump(obj` or `write_json(`. A file that writes no object is not a writer whose guard status could mean anything; it is not in the population at all. The absence here selects the denominator rather than hiding a defect, and the denominator IS the headline number the run prints on every execution -- 70 writers, of which 2 import a do-not-rebuild check and 68 do not. That figure would be meaningless if non-writers were counted, and it is stated rather than implied, so the set that was skipped is visible as arithmetic. The property this instrument actually reports on -- an UNCONDITIONAL assignment to `manuscript.<field>` -- is computed positively and currently measures 0 of 2, both guarded.

rebaselined_2026_08_20: A BASELINE KEYED ON file:line CANNOT SURVIVE AN EDIT ABOVE THE LINE. Six-line docstring notes were added to lint_method_claim_has_a_field.py, lint_no_false_allclear.py and lint_self_describing_safety_claim.py recording that each had been PROVEN BY GRAFT. Every negative guard below those insertions shifted -- 217/220/227 -> 223/226/233, 102 -> 108, 74 -> 80 -- and re-read as NEW while the same number vanished as HEALED. Nine gone, eight new, and not one line of guard logic changed. THE KEY DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE THING IT NAMES, which is the same family as lint 50 storing a COUNT of claims rather than the claims: both detect movement and are blind to what moved. Keying on the guard text plus its enclosing function would survive an edit above it. Recorded, not fixed.

notes.lint_collinear_protocol.py: Both are iteration filters, not absence-claims. The first selects .py files to walk; the second skips a file the scanner returned no hit for. Neither concludes anything FROM an absence -- the instrument's finding is a positive match (a rater collection subscripted by a counter modulo n), and its four controls assert that a known-confounded file is CAUGHT and a fully-crossed one is CLEAN. notes.lane_rob/gate_estimate_reconciles.py: Not an exclusion-by-absence: the guard classifies a row INTO a named state (PARTIAL, 'events present, treatment N absent') and records the reason, rather than dropping it from a denominator. why_each_absence_is_the_property_2026_08.scripts/rederive_no_information_domains_: SEVEN GUARDS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS A DECISION. Six are shape guards -- `not isinstance(dv/per/rec/rb, dict)`, `not isinstance(stored_j, str)`, `not os.path.isfile(p)`. A value that is not a dict is not a domain record and a path that is not a file is not an object; the absence IS the property, and there is no positive form of `this is a domain record` that the schema supplies. THE SEVENTH IS THE REAL ONE: `if q is None` fires when a NO_INFORMATION domain has neither stored signalling answers nor a declared ceiling, so no responses can be assembled and the published algorithm cannot be run on it. It does NOT narrow the pass: the branch increments `tier['no basis -- left untouched']` and a per-domain entry in `gaps`, both printed every run, and the domain is left exactly as it was. That is the distinction this ratchet exists to force -- a skip that is COUNTED and NAMED is not the `zero paper-* sections` failure, which was a skip nobody could see. If this branch ever starts writing a value instead of counting one, it must leave the baseline and be argued again.
